question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=50$ from a population where $20%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that between $15%$ and $25%$ of the sample have the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=50,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.2.$

Now, since

$$
np=50(0.2)=10>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=50(1-0.2)=40>5,
$$

and $n=50$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.2,\frac{0.2(1-0.2)}{50}) \\  & ∼N(0.2,0.0032).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(0.15\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.25).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.15\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.25) & =P(\frac{0.15-0.2}{\sqrt{0.0032}}\le Z\le \frac{0.25-0.2}{\sqrt{0.0032}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.88\le Z\le 0.88) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.88)-P(Z\le -0.88) \\  & =Φ(0.88)-Φ(-0.88)\end{aligned}
$$
